title: Watch-out notes before you start
problem: The app remembers where every note has been landing, but shows it only on the Progress tab. Before a run, the practice page shows plain note names, so a habit like a sharp second finger only comes up again after the run is over.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The Progress tab's note map averages each note's last 20 landings and says: "Consistent bars one side = a habit to fix."
Before a run, the practice page's note strip draws each note as a plain chip with its name and octave, and no history.
The coach's notes look for habits only in the run just played, once it is over.

hypothesis: If the practice page names the note in this drill you have been landing off lately, and which way to move, you fix it on the first try instead of after a missed run.
acceptance_criteria: Before a run, when a note in the selected drill has averaged 6 cents or more off, on the same side, over its recent landings, a Watch line under the note strip names it, the amount and which way to move.
That note's chip is marked sharp or flat.
Nothing shows for a drill with no consistent miss, and nothing changes during a run.
The line updates after every run.
success_signal: Fewer first-try misses on flagged notes over the next two weeks, in the practice log.
strongest_reason_not_to_build: It adds words to the practice screen, and a warning before you play can make you tense and over-correct. The Progress tab already shows the same history.
